Makkan, and it has two hundred and forty-seven letters, fifty-four words and fifteen verses.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi informed me, saying: Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hamid informed us, saying:

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Asbahani related to us, saying: al-Mu'ammil ibn Isma'il related to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri related to us, saying: Aslam al-Minqari related to us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayzi, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah "Wa-sh-Shams," it is as if he has given in charity everything that the sun and the moon have risen upon" [153] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/367.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾. Mujahid said: its light. Qatadah: it is the whole day. Muqatil: its heat, as in His saying in Ta-Ha: ﴿nor be scorched by the sun﴾ [[Surah Ta-Ha: 119.]], meaning the heat will not harm you.

﴿And by the moon when it follows it﴾: it follows it, takes from its light and travels behind it. That occurs in the first half of the month, when the sun sets and the moon rises after it.

﴿And by the day when it displays it﴾: it displays the sun, revealing it by its illumination. Al-Farra' and a group of scholars said: it means "and by the day when it displays the darkness," so the pronoun refers to darkness without it having been mentioned earlier, because its meaning is known. Do you not see that you say: "The morning was cold, the evening was harsh, and the north wind blew," thus referring to feminine things that have not been mentioned, because their meaning is known.

﴿And by the night when it covers it﴾, i.e., it covers the sun until it sets, so the horizons become dark [[See Lisan al-Arab: 14/153, entry "ajlā".]].

﴿And by the sky and He who built it﴾, i.e., and He who created it, namely Allah, the Exalted, as in His saying: ﴿so marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 3.]]. It was also said: "ma" is a verbal noun, meaning "and its building," as in His saying: ﴿by what my Lord forgave me﴾ [[Surah Ya-Sin: 27.]]. ﴿And by the earth and He who spread it out﴾: He created what is in it. Related from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, and al-Walibi from him: he divided it. Another said: He spread it out. ﴿And by the soul and He who proportioned it﴾: He made its creation balanced. ﴿And inspired it with its wickedness and its piety﴾. Ibn Abbas, by the narration of al-Walibi, said: He shows it the good and the evil.

Al-Awfi related from him: He taught it obedience and disobedience. Al-Kalbi: He informed it of what will come and what ought to be. Ibn Zayd and Ibn al-Fadl said: He placed this in it, meaning by His granting it success toward piety and His abandonment of it toward wickedness.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Azrah ibn Thabit al-Ansari related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Uqayl related to us, from Yahya ibn Ya'mar, from Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali, who said: Imran ibn Husayn said to me: "Have you considered what people work at and strive over? Is it a thing that has been decreed upon them and has passed over them from a predestined decree, or is it concerning what they will face of what their Prophet (ﷺ) brought them, and the proof has been established against them?" I said: "Everything has been decreed upon them." He said: "Would that be injustice?" I was greatly alarmed by it and said: "There is nothing except that He created it and it is under His dominion. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned" [[Surah al-Anbiya': 23.]]. He said to me: "May Allah keep you upright. Have you considered what people work at and strive over? Is it a thing decreed upon them from a predestined decree, or is it concerning what they will face of what their Prophet (ﷺ) brought, by which the proof has been established against them?"

He said: "It concerns a thing that has been decreed upon them." I said: "Then the work is completed, when he whom Allah, the Exalted, created for one of the two stations, Allah prepares him for it, and the confirmation of this is in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and the soul and He who proportioned it, and inspired it with its wickedness and its piety﴾."

﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾: he prospered and won, and here is the place of the oath. ﴿Purifies it﴾, i.e., the soul has succeeded that Allah purified, meaning He set it right, cleansed it of sins, and granted it success in piety. ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾: the soul has lost that Allah corrupted, meaning He left it neglected and abandoned it, lowered it, and concealed its station, when it worked at wickedness and committed sins. The Arabs do this often, changing one of the letters of a doubled (shaddah) root into a yā' or wāw, as in "al-taqaddi" and "al-tazannī" and their kind.

Abu Bakr ibn Ayluwas informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahfuzi informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid:

﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾: one of them said: he set it right; the other said: he purified it.

﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾: one of them said: he led it astray; the other said: he misguided it. Qatadah said: "dassaha" means he made it sinful and wicked. Ibn Abbas said: he nullified it and destroyed it.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Muzani informed us, saying: al-Hadrami related to us, saying: Uthman related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Salih: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it﴾: "The soul has succeeded that Allah purified, and the soul has failed that Allah corrupted, Mighty and Majestic."

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: He has certainly succeeded who purifies his soul, setting it right and bringing it to obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; ﴿and he has failed who corrupts it﴾: he who destroys it, misguides it, and drives it to disobedience of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Thus he made the action belong to the soul.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: al-Yaqtini related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-'Uqayli informed us, saying: Safwan ibn Salih related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he recited this verse, ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾, would pause and then say: "O Allah, grant my soul its piety; You are its Guardian and its Lord, and purify it, for You are the best of those who purify it" [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/209.]].
